Develop and implement site-specific security strategies aligned with corporate security policies
Develop multi-year physical security plans that address current operations, future facility expansion, government programs, and evolving threats
Maintain security plans, post orders, procedures, and operating instructions
Conduct periodic security risk assessments and vulnerability reviews
Oversee day-to-day security operations and site access control
Be the primary point of contact for security incidents and coordinate response activities
Manage contracted security service providers and guard force personnel
Coordinate and manage test exclusion areas that extend into public spaces
Support security requirements associated with classified contracts, cleared programs, secure facilities, and government customer activites
Oversee operation and maintenance of access control systems, CCTV and video management systems, intrusion detection systems, and perimeter security systems.
Serve as the primary security liaison with government organizations, law enforcement agencies, port authorities, and emergency management organizations
Coordinate site access requirements, special events, test operations, and security-related government activities
Lead investigations involving security violations, theft, property damage, unauthorized access, workplace violence concerns, suspicious activity
Support site emergency preparedness and response planning
Develop and deliver security awareness training

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience
5+ years of experience in physical security, law enforcement, military security, industrial security, or related field
3+ years of leadership experience managing security personnel or security programs
Demonstrated experience establishing physical security programs, including security strategy, policies, staffing models, and security infrastructure
Experience managing contract guard force operations
Experience with enterprise access control and video surveillance systems
Strong incident management and investigation skills
Ability to obtain and maintain required security clearances if necessary
Valid state security officer license, or eligibility to obtain one
Valid driver's license
Strong communication and customer service skills
Ability to routinely walk, patrol, and inspect large industrial, manufacturing, and test facilities, including climbing stairs, ladders, and elevated platforms
Ability to work in outdoor and industrial environments, including construction zones in varying weather conditions, and while wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE)
Ability to respond to security incidents and emergencies anywhere on site, including working extended hours, nights, weekends, and test operations as required
Ability to hold and maintain a Federal DBIDS including ability to pass USSF background
Ability to hold and maintain a TWIC card
Willing to relocate to Kent, WA

Preferred Qualifications

Aerospace, defense, launch operations, manufacturing, critical infrastructure, or maritime experience
Experience working within the National Industrial Security Program or other federal security environment
Experience interfacing with the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency
Familiarity with facility clearance and industrial security requirements, including the NISPOM
Experience operating within federal or military environments
Experience supporting government customers and regulatory agencies
Security certifications such as PSP (Physical Security Professional), CPP (Certified Protection Professional), ASIS certifications, FEMA Incident Command certifications
Secret (or higher) security clearance level

Benefits

Equity – We know that our employees are the reason we succeed. To give everyone a stake in our future, we are pleased to offer equity in the form of stock options to all regular, full-time employees.
Comprehensive benefits program including subsidized medical, dental, and vision insurance
Company-paid life and disability insurance
401(k) plan with employer match
4 weeks’ Paid Time Off
Holidays – 10 days (including an end-of-year closure)
Paid Family/Parental Leave
On-site gym or monthly wellness stipend (depending on location)
Dog friendly offices!

Compensation

Level 4: $92,610 - $138,810

jobs.title: Senior Field Project Manager
Senior Program Manager I - Laser Communications
jobs.description:
About Rocket Lab

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we’re building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, laser communication terminals, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

SENIOR PROGRAM MANAGER I - LASER COMMUNICATIONS

Laser communication is the backbone of the constellations of today and tomorrow, and demand for it is growing fast. We are scaling industry-leading optical communication terminals to meet it: high-performing, affordable, and available at the volume commercial and government constellation operators need. Based at Rocket Lab’s global headquarters in Long Beach, CA, you are the customer’s champion and the delivery lead for our optical communication terminal programs. You own the customer outcome: the day-to-day relationship, delivery commitments and schedule at rate, milestone and acceptance reviews, risk, and program health. You build on a proven, standard terminal product and partner closely with our Product team on configuration, pricing, and new customer needs. You’ll work alongside the teams that build the spacecraft, the components, and the rockets, so the people you need to solve a problem are down the hall, not under another contract. This is a high-impact, customer-facing role: you connect the customer, our engineering teams, the production line, and the business across two continents, and you’re the person our customers count on.

What You'll Get To Do

Lead Delivery: Lead terminal programs from award through qualification, production at rate, delivery, and on-orbit checkout, across current-generation production and next-generation variants. Hold each program to its plan and deliver on schedule, technical performance, and every customer commitment.
Lead the Team of Teams: Run multiple concurrent customer programs, work closely with Chief Engineers on link performance, data rate, SWaP, environmental qualification, and optical terminal interoperability, and dive in personally on the problems that matter most to delivery.
Deliver at Rate: Own each program’s delivery profile and protect it. Spot yield, supplier, and test-capacity risk early and drive it to closure with Operations and the Product team.
Forge the Supply Chain: Partner with Supply Chain to manage critical suppliers as strategic partners, building the relationships and accountability that keep every customer delivery on schedule.
Run the Program Lifecycle: Own program startup and baselining, milestone and qualification reviews, export and ITAR obligations with Trade Compliance, customer acceptance, and closeout across our U.S. and European sites.
Champion the Customer: Be the trusted point of contact for customers through milestone reviews, interoperability campaigns, acceptance, and delivery. Partner with BD & Strategy on proposals and with the Product team on pricing and configuration, bringing the voice of the customer to every decision.
Raise the Bar: Mentor the people around you, set a high standard for how we show up for customers, and help develop the program leaders who will run our next generation of laser communications programs.

You'll Bring These Qualifications As Senior Program Manager i

Engineering Foundation: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Physics, or Math.
Technical Depth: Working understanding of free-space optical or RF communications: link budgets, pointing, acquisition, and tracking, modems and coding, and space or airborne environmental qualification.
5+ years in space, aerospace, or photonics hardware programs, with multiple full program cycles. We weight the hardest thing you’ve shipped over the count.
Customer Delivery: A track record of leading a complex hardware program to delivery (customer, schedule, risk, and acceptance) and carrying it across the finish line under real pressure.
Production Delivery: Evidence you’ve moved real hardware from prototype to qualified, rate-production delivery to customers.
Program Financials: Experience managing program cost, EAC, and customer contract changes in partnership with finance and product teams on a program of meaningful scale.
Proof Point: You’ve delivered hardware at rate to a demanding customer and kept their trust through a hard moment, such as a slip, a test failure, or a contract change.
Clearance: U.S. Person status required (ITAR/EAR); ability to obtain a security clearance preferred.

These Qualifications Would Be Nice To Have

Domain Authority: Direct experience with optical inter-satellite links or optical ground or airborne terminals.
Production Velocity: A proven playbook for taking low-volume, hand-built optical or electro-optical hardware into high-rate production without sacrificing reliability.
Constellation Fluency: Experience delivering to large commercial or defense constellation programs.
Customer Leadership: Experience as the primary customer interface for constellation operators or satellite primes, from kickoff through acceptance.
Global Leadership: Experience leading program work across geographically dispersed sites, including export-control and dual-use compliance.
Advanced Technical Credibility: A Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Optics/Photonics, Physics, or a related field.
Systems & Toolchain Fluency: You speak systems engineering (trade studies, interface control, requirement integrity) and use Jira, Confluence, and ERP/MRP to keep program health visible at speed.
AI Fluency: You put AI tools to work in day-to-day program management, from schedule and risk analysis to status reporting and customer communications, so you and your team spend more time on the problems that matter.

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Anticipated annual equity grant value is designed around function, level, experience, and other factors; realized value depends on vesting and stock-price performance.Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Total Compensation (base and equity): $137,075 USD - $196,275 USD

Base Salary: $116,800 USD - $160,600 USD

What To Expect

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

jobs.title: Space All-Source Intelligence Analyst
jobs.description:
Description

Are you passionate about using intelligence analysis to solve complex challenges in the space domain?

Do you enjoy turning intelligence from multiple sources into actionable data that can inform modeling, simulation, and analysis?

Are you interested in working alongside engineers, modelers, and analysts to help assess and forecast national security space threats?

If so, we're looking for someone like you to join our team at APL!

We are seeking a Space All-Source Intelligence Analyst to support programs within APL's National Security Space Mission Area (NSSMA). You will apply your knowledge of the Intelligence Community (IC) and experience with all-source intelligence analysis to help address critical challenges facing the Department of Defense (DoD) and Intelligence Community in the space domain.

In this role, you will serve as a critical link between intelligence and the technical teams developing high-fidelity modeling, simulation, and analysis (MS&A) capabilities. Rather than focusing primarily on traditional intelligence reporting, you will acquire, analyze, and translate intelligence from multiple classified sources into the quantitative data, parameters, and operational context needed to develop realistic models and simulations. You will collaborate closely with systems engineers, modelers, data scientists, and program teams to ensure our analyses accurately represent real-world threats and operating environments.

As a Space All-Source Intelligence Analyst, you will...

Acquire, analyze, and synthesize intelligence from multiple sources and classified disciplines to develop a comprehensive understanding of space threats and operational environments.
Translate qualitative intelligence assessments into quantitative data, variables, and parameters that can be incorporated into modeling, simulation, and analysis tools.
Collaborate with systems engineers and modelers to integrate intelligence into high-fidelity models used to assess and forecast national security space threats.
Apply intelligence insights to develop realistic operational and training scenarios for complex simulations.
Support model verification and validation by comparing simulation results with available real-world intelligence and identifying discrepancies that may affect model accuracy or fidelity.
Develop and maintain detailed threat and operational environment profiles to ensure models and simulations reflect the most current intelligence available.
Work closely with MS&A engineers, data scientists, analysts, and program managers to define intelligence requirements and effectively integrate intelligence throughout the modeling and analysis lifecycle.
Communicate intelligence findings and technical insights to multidisciplinary teams to support analyses, assessments, and sponsor needs.

Qualifications

You meet our minimum qualifications for the job if you...

B.S. in Intelligence Studies, Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, Data Science or equivalent experience.
At least 5 years of experience in DoD and IC-developed space systems, especially those systems focused on space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR), and space situational awareness (SSA)
Expert with IC and DoD processes and protocols for intelligence sharing and collaboration
Demonstrated experience conducting all-source analysis, data and intelligence synthesis, and intelligence analysis and production
Strong written and verbal communication skills with experience preparing executive-level reports, briefings, and intelligence-product publications
Hold an active TS/SCI security clearance. If selected, you will be subject to a government security clearance investigation and must meet the requirements for access to classified information. Eligibility requirements include U.S. citizenship.

You'll go above and beyond our minimum requirements if you...

Advanced degree in Intelligence Studies, National Security, National Strategy, Space Systems Engineering, or related STEM with 8+ years of relevant experience
Assignments to various IC organizations, with at least 3+ years at any one
Demonstrated experience working Space Weapons and Tactics
Experience in Red Team methodologies and threat analysis approaches
Participation in Space Warfare games (i.e., THORS HAMMER, Schriever Wargames, Space Flag)
Current TS//SCI clearance with polygraph, and with existing or previous access to SAP/CAP programs.

About Us

Why Work at APL?

The Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) brings world-class expertise to our nation’s most critical defense, security, space and science challenges. While we are dedicated to solving complex challenges and pioneering new technologies, what makes us truly outstanding is our culture. We offer a vibrant, welcoming atmosphere where you can bring your authentic self to work, continue to grow, and build strong connections with inspiring teammates.

At APL, we celebrate our differences of perspectives and encourage creativity and bold, new ideas. Our employees enjoy generous benefits, including a robust education assistance program, unparalleled retirement contributions, and a healthy work/life balance. jobs.description:
Description

Amazon is the most customer-centric company on Earth. We need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people who are passionate about doing the right thing.

We are looking for a Business Intelligence Analyst to join the Pricing & Payments team within Amazon's Last Mile Brazil organization, as part of the Partner Strategy & Experience (PSX) organization. This role owns the design, development, and maintenance of data intelligence solutions, automated mechanisms, and analytical frameworks that ensure pricing accuracy, payment reliability, and financial health across all delivery partner programs — EDSP (External Delivery Service Provider), AMPL (Amazon Partner Logistics), and AMXL (Amazon Extra Large).

As an Individual Contributor, you will be the data and automation backbone of the Payments & Pricing function — building pipelines, dashboards, reconciliation mechanisms, and self-service tools that eliminate manual processes, reduce payment errors, and provide real-time visibility into financial operations. You will partner closely with Payments Specialists, Pricing Specialists, Finance, and Operations to turn complex data into actionable intelligence.

This role reports directly to the Pricing & Payments Manager and works cross-functionally with Finance, Operations, Technology, and partner-facing teams.

This position is based out of an AMZL office.

If you are passionate about building intelligent data solutions, automating complex processes, and driving financial precision through analytics, come join our team.

Key job responsibilities

Design, build, and maintain automated data pipelines and ETL processes that support payment reconciliation, pricing validation, and financial reporting across all partner programs

Develop and maintain SQL-based queries, views, and stored procedures to extract, transform, and analyze large-scale operational and financial datasets

Build and maintain dashboards and reporting mechanisms (QuickSight, Tableau, or equivalent) providing real-time visibility into payment status, pricing accuracy, disputes, and financial KPIs

Create automated reconciliation mechanisms that identify payment discrepancies, pricing errors, and anomalies before they impact partners — reducing manual intervention and improving trust

Develop self-service analytical tools that enable the Payments and Pricing team to access insights without requiring ad-hoc requests

Automate recurring reports and manual processes, driving efficiency gains across the Payments & Pricing function

Conduct deep-dive analyses on payment cycles, dispute patterns, incentive effectiveness, and pricing model performance to support data-driven decision-making

Build alerting and exception-handling mechanisms that proactively flag issues (e.g., payment delays, pricing inconsistencies, unusual dispute volumes)

Partner with Technology and Engineering teams to define data requirements, validate data sources, and ensure data quality and integrity

Support the development of pricing models and incentive simulations by providing historical data analysis, scenario modeling, and impact projections

Document all data solutions, pipelines, and mechanisms with clear technical specifications and operational runbooks

Present analytical findings and automation proposals to stakeholders, translating technical solutions into business value

A day in the life

Your day starts by checking the automated health monitors you built for the payment pipeline. An alert fires — a batch of AMPL partner payments shows a 3% discrepancy against expected values. You dive into the SQL query that powers the reconciliation engine, identify a data source lag from a route restructuring, and push a fix before the payment cycle closes.

Mid-morning, you join a sync with the Payments Specialists to review a new automated dispute detection mechanism you're piloting. The early results are promising: 40% of disputes that previously required manual review are now auto-classified and routed, saving 15+ hours per week.

Before lunch, you finalize a new QuickSight dashboard for the Pricing team — it visualizes incentive effectiveness across partner segments, showing which incentive structures drive the best delivery performance per Real invested. You walk the Pricing Specialist through the self-service filters and drill-down capabilities.

After lunch, you deep-dive into a request from the Ops Excellence Manager: they need historical payment data cross-referenced with partner Scorecard performance to validate a hypothesis about payment timeliness and delivery quality correlation. You build the query, visualize the results, and share a brief with your findings.

Late afternoon, you work on your current sprint priority: automating the monthly partner payment summary that currently takes 8 hours of manual work. You're building a Python script that pulls from three data sources, reconciles automatically, and generates the formatted output — target: zero manual hours by next month.

You close the day documenting the new pipeline you deployed this week and updating the team's automation roadmap with next quarter's priorities.

About The Team

The Business Intelligence Analyst sits within the Pricing & Payments team, part of Amazon Logistics' Partner Strategy & Experience (PSX) organization. The Pricing & Payments function owns one of PSX's core pillars: "Pricing accuracy, incentive effectiveness, and payment reliability: ensuring financial health and trust across all delivery channels."

The team manages pricing models, payment cycles, incentive structures, and dispute resolution for +30 logistics partners across Brazil. The BI Analyst is the technical engine of this function — building the data infrastructure, automations, and intelligence that enable the team to operate at scale with precision and speed.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience in Business, Engineering, Supply Chain, Transportation, Mathematics, Economics, Physics or another technical field
Knowledge of writing and optimizing SQL queries in a business environment with large-scale, complex datasets
Experience building data pipelines or automated ETL processes
Experience with reporting and Data Visualization tools such as Quick Sight / Tableau / Power BI or other BI packages
Experience with data scripting languages (e.g., SQL, Python, R, or equivalent) or statistical/mathematical software (e.g., R, SAS, Matlab, or equivalent)
Experience in translating business needs into detailed feature requirements
Experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities, or experience in SQL Server/MySQL
Experience communicating technical concepts to non-technical audiences
Experience in communication and presentation skills, both written and verbal in Portuguese & English

Preferred Qualifications

Speak, write, and read fluently in English
Experience with financial services, payments or e-commerce
Experience with creating automated alarms, reports and KPI metrics for plant management
Knowledge of finance, accounting, business or related field focused on analytics
Experience working with Git or an equivalent distributed version control system
Experience in program management, logistics, operations, supply chain, transportation, or equivalent
Experience automating routine tasks
Knowledge of data structures, data modeling, and database schema
Master's degree in Math, Statistics, Computer Science, or related science field, or Master's degree and 2+ years of data scientist experience
Experience in Amazon Redshift and other AWS technologies

jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager, WW Benchmarking and Scorecard (GSCE)

Description

Amazon's Global Standards & Customer Excellence (GSCE) organization owns the Worldwide Scorecard - the mechanism that provides a holistic view of operational performance across Safety, People, Customer Experience, Quality, Cost, and Sustainability pillars for 1,000+ last-mile delivery stations and sort centers spanning North America, Europe, Japan, India, and ECCF. The WW Benchmarking team within GSCE manages performance benchmarking using the Continuous Benchmarking Rate Setting (CBRS) methodology - clustering stations into peer groups and setting statistically rigorous performance targets that control for non-ops factors.

As the Senior Program Manager for the Quality Pillar, you will own end-to-end benchmarking and scorecard strategy for First Pass Yield (FPY), Stow Buffer Compliance, and emerging quality metrics across all regions. You will drive the CBRS methodology for quality KPIs, launch and scale benchmarking studies that close performance gaps at underperforming stations, develop next-generation metrics that replace legacy measurements, and feed input-level KPIs into the Risk Engine that powers predictive operational alerts. You will partner with Operations, ACES, BIE (Analytics), and Finance teams to ensure quality benchmarks are accurate, equitable, and drive measurable operational improvement across stations worldwide.

This role requires strong analytical thinking, program management rigor, and the ability to translate complex statistical methodologies into operator-friendly insights. You will manage multiple concurrent workstreams - from quarterly benchmark refreshes, to multi-month benchmarking studies with site-level interventions, to expanding quality benchmarks to new regions and business units where none previously existed. You will also build AI-powered tooling that accelerates validation and delivery, and contribute input signals to the Gravion Risk Engine. Cross-team coordination, data fluency, stakeholder communication to senior leadership, and a bias for automation are essential.

You will be a strong partner of Central and Field ACES teams - delivering operator sentiment of the metrics, benchmarking the metrics and aligning closely with their OP process, initiating metric changes, and maintaining metric parity around the world.

Key job responsibilities

Own the Quality Pillar benchmarking portfolio end-to-end — vision, methodology, and cadence for FPY, Stow Buffer Compliance, and future quality metrics across NA, EU, JP, ECCF, RSR, and RoW
Drive benchmarking methodology for quality KPIs — quarterly benchmark generation, cluster design, sub-cluster coefficients, and statistical model improvement
Design benchmarking studies identifying root causes at underperforming stations, sharing best practices, and driving measurable quality improvement
Expand quality benchmarks to new regions and BUs — adapting methodology for local data, gaining alignment, and launching benchmarks where none existed
Own Road to CBRS (benchmarking) for quality metrics — translating benchmarks into actionable station-level insights that close the gap
Partner with Central and Field ACES on operator sentiment, OP alignment, and worldwide metric parity
Define upstream quality KPI signals for the Risk Engine — early-warning indicators and data integration partnership
Build AI-powered validation tooling — cluster analyzers, anomaly detection, and self-service analytics for operators
Partner with BIE on data pipeline requirements — freshness, accuracy, and scalability in Andes/Redshift
Present insights, study results, and methodology recommendations to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders
Write quality pillar narratives for quarterly publications and stakeholder newsletters

A day in the life

Monday: Review CBRS cluster refresh — identify sub-cluster movements, flag quality KPI anomalies, prep stakeholder insights. Tuesday: Triage Asana intakes, meet operators to answer benchmark and cluster placement questions.
Mid-week: Strategic alignment with stakeholders on metric logic, long-term vision, and network performance. Meet cross-BU stakeholders on benchmarking expansion needs for quality metrics.
Thursday: Deep methodology work — review site outliers per Quality Pillar KPI, discuss logic changes with regional stakeholders, assess network impact.
Friday: Document weekly quality benchmarking performance, update study progress, share best practices from top stations, field operator gap-closure questions.

About The Team

The WW Benchmarking & Standards team establishes the performance truth for Amazon's global last mile network — defining what "good" looks like across 1,000+ delivery stations through statistically validated benchmarks and engineering-grade standards. We set the rates that drive labor planning decisions, publish the WW Scorecard that holds stations accountable to peer-adjusted targets, and run multi-month benchmarking studies that convert underperformance into quantified improvement opportunities.

jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager, WW Benchmarking and Scorecard (GSCE)
jobs.description:
Description

Amazon's Global Standards & Customer Excellence (GSCE) organization owns the Worldwide Scorecard - the mechanism that provides a holistic view of operational performance across Safety, People, Customer Experience, Quality, Cost, and Sustainability pillars for 1,000+ last-mile delivery stations and sort centers spanning North America, Europe, Japan, India, and ECCF. The WW Benchmarking team within GSCE manages performance benchmarking using the Continuous Benchmarking Rate Setting (CBRS) methodology - clustering stations into peer groups and setting statistically rigorous performance targets that control for non-ops factors.

As the Senior Program Manager for the Quality Pillar, you will own end-to-end benchmarking and scorecard strategy for First Pass Yield (FPY), Stow Buffer Compliance, and emerging quality metrics across all regions. You will drive the CBRS methodology for quality KPIs, launch and scale benchmarking studies that close performance gaps at underperforming stations, develop next-generation metrics that replace legacy measurements, and feed input-level KPIs into the Risk Engine that powers predictive operational alerts. You will partner with Operations, ACES, BIE (Analytics), and Finance teams to ensure quality benchmarks are accurate, equitable, and drive measurable operational improvement across stations worldwide.

This role requires strong analytical thinking, program management rigor, and the ability to translate complex statistical methodologies into operator-friendly insights. You will manage multiple concurrent workstreams - from quarterly benchmark refreshes, to multi-month benchmarking studies with site-level interventions, to expanding quality benchmarks to new regions and business units where none previously existed. You will also build AI-powered tooling that accelerates validation and delivery, and contribute input signals to the Gravion Risk Engine. Cross-team coordination, data fluency, stakeholder communication to senior leadership, and a bias for automation are essential.

You will be a strong partner of Central and Field ACES teams - delivering operator sentiment of the metrics, benchmarking the metrics and aligning closely with their OP process, initiating metric changes, and maintaining metric parity around the world.

Key job responsibilities

Own the Quality Pillar benchmarking portfolio end-to-end — vision, methodology, and cadence for FPY, Stow Buffer Compliance, and future quality metrics across NA, EU, JP, ECCF, RSR, and RoW
Drive benchmarking methodology for quality KPIs — quarterly benchmark generation, cluster design, sub-cluster coefficients, and statistical model improvement
Design benchmarking studies identifying root causes at underperforming stations, sharing best practices, and driving measurable quality improvement
Expand quality benchmarks to new regions and BUs — adapting methodology for local data, gaining alignment, and launching benchmarks where none existed
Own Road to CBRS (benchmarking) for quality metrics — translating benchmarks into actionable station-level insights that close the gap
Partner with Central and Field ACES on operator sentiment, OP alignment, and worldwide metric parity
Define upstream quality KPI signals for the Risk Engine — early-warning indicators and data integration partnership
Build AI-powered validation tooling — cluster analyzers, anomaly detection, and self-service analytics for operators
Partner with BIE on data pipeline requirements — freshness, accuracy, and scalability in Andes/Redshift
Present insights, study results, and methodology recommendations to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders
Write quality pillar narratives for quarterly publications and stakeholder newsletters

A day in the life

Monday: Review CBRS cluster refresh — identify sub-cluster movements, flag quality KPI anomalies, prep stakeholder insights. Tuesday: Triage Asana intakes, meet operators to answer benchmark and cluster placement questions.
Mid-week: Strategic alignment with stakeholders on metric logic, long-term vision, and network performance. Meet cross-BU stakeholders on benchmarking expansion needs for quality metrics.
Thursday: Deep methodology work — review site outliers per Quality Pillar KPI, discuss logic changes with regional stakeholders, assess network impact.
Friday: Document weekly quality benchmarking performance, update study progress, share best practices from top stations, field operator gap-closure questions.

Amazon offers a full range of benefits that support you and eligible family members, including domestic partners and their children. Benefits can vary by location, the number of regularly scheduled hours you work, length of employment, and job status such as seasonal or temporary employment.

The benefits that generally apply to regular, full-time employees include:

Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage
Maternity and Parental Leave Options
Paid Time Off (PTO)
401(k) Plan

If you are not sure that every qualification on the list above describes you exactly, we'd still love to hear from you!

At Amazon, we value people with unique backgrounds, experiences, and skillsets. If you’re passionate about this role and want to make an impact on a global scale, please apply!

About The Team

The WW Benchmarking & Standards team establishes the performance truth for Amazon's global last mile network — defining what "good" looks like across 1,000+ delivery stations through statistically validated benchmarks and engineering-grade standards. We set the rates that drive labor planning decisions, publish the WW Scorecard that holds stations accountable to peer-adjusted targets, and run multi-month benchmarking studies that convert underperformance into quantified improvement opportunities.

Our CBRS methodology clusters stations into statistically comparable peer groups, removing excuses and surfacing true operational gaps. We are expanding from retrospective measurement into predictive performance engineering — building risk engines, self-service analytics, and AI-powered tooling that tell operators not just where they stand, but what to do next. The team operates at the intersection of data science, program management, and field operations.

Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience implementing repeatable processes and driving automation or standardization
5+ years of managing, analyzing and communicating results to senior leadership experience

Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field
Knowledge of general AI tools
Experience designing, implementing, and scaling upskilling, apprenticeship, or workforce development programs across large-scale operations or corporate environments, including forecasting workforce needs and leveraging analytics to drive program decisions
PMP certificate

Working cross-functionally with Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Quality, Finance, Product Management, Business Development, and customers, the Senior Program Manager supports strategic program execution, customer relationship management, risk mitigation, and operational performance while ensuring programs are delivered in accordance with contractual requirements, financial objectives, and customer expectations.

Lead execution of complex, high-value programs by developing integrated program strategies, execution plans, schedules, milestones, and performance objectives.
Evaluate program performance across cost, schedule, technical, quality, and contractual requirements while implementing strategies that improve execution and customer satisfaction.
Oversee successful execution of product development, manufacturing, production, integration, and customer delivery activities.
Provide strategic direction that ensures alignment between program objectives and organizational priorities.
Serve as the primary customer interface for complex programs and strategic customer engagements.
Lead customer program reviews, executive briefings, milestone reviews, and contractual discussions.
Build long-term relationships with customers that strengthen confidence, program execution, and future business opportunities.
Communicate program performance, risks, financial status, and strategic recommendations to executive leadership and customers.
Lead integrated program teams across Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Quality, Finance, Product Management, and Business Development.
Evaluate program risks, dependencies, resource constraints, and business impacts while implementing mitigation strategies.
Coordinate proposal transition, contract execution, production readiness, product delivery, and lifecycle support activities.
Influence cross-functional decision-making to achieve successful program outcomes.
Spearhead initiatives that strengthen program management processes, execution methodologies, and operational effectiveness.
Develop integrated program management frameworks, reporting tools, governance processes, and performance metrics.
Support continuous improvement initiatives that improve program execution, customer satisfaction, and business performance.
Ensure compliance with contractual requirements, company procedures, and customer expectations.

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business Administration, Program Management, Operations Management, Supply Chain, or a related field with 12–15 years of related experience, or a Master's degree with 8–12 years of related experience in program management, project management, operations, engineering, manufacturing, or a related discipline.

Troubleshoot fee execution issues through thoughtful data analysis and understanding of firm systems.
Collaborate with internal and external clients on execution of fee agreements to meet multiple team goals.

Administration of approved alternative fee arrangements in our accounting system (3E) to ensure accurate and timely billing while meeting firm standards.
Monitoring and triaging incoming requests and questions from centralized team mailbox.
Design, build, and implement tools and process to better control and maintenance of AFAs.
Review new matter openings and ensure approved pricing is applied in accounting system timely and accurately.
Analyze firm portfolio of AFAs to drive decisions on firm approval of AFAs.
Advise on opportunities to improve data and processes to reduce configuration time and prevent fee losses.
Assist with the yearly price renewal process by reviewing current AFAs and auditing terms for accuracy.

Experience and interest in extracting and reporting of data using standard query language (SQL) is highly desired.
Strong analytical and critical thinking skills.
Requires a strong work ethic; ability to quickly adapt to shifting priorities, capable of carrying out routine, everyday tasks with limited direction/supervision.
Ability to work outside of established business hours and adjust personal schedule to meet deadlines is required.

jobs.title: PROJECT MANAGER
jobs.description:
Job Summary

This position is located in the District Department of Transportation (DDOT), Transportation Planning Administration (TPA), Curbside Management Division (CMD). Incumbent serves as a project manager for Curbside Management Division initiatives that span across CMD branches and across the agency and require coordination with external stakeholders and other District government agencies. The incumbent will perform and delegate a wide variety of assignments relative to the development and implementation of policies, strategies, work plans, implementation processes, and quality control measures to ensure strategic curbside management initiatives are successfully implemented. Example initiatives could include implementing citywide paid parking signage updates, expanding performance parking zones, or launching an automated curbside management and enforcement system.

The incumbent is responsible for formulating plans and processes to equitably deliver a safe, sustainable, and reliable multimodal transportation network for all, by creating a dynamic, equitable, and accessible curbside and urban delivery environment that reliably serves residents, businesses, and visitors. The incumbent serves as an expert consultant in all areas affected by assigned projects and must propose new methods of maintaining the agency's mission. The work includes the smooth delivery of major transportation and infrastructure projects within specific geographical areas of the District.

Duties And Responsibilities

Directs and oversee a portfolio of complex and major capital projects in a designated geographic area and assigned by the Deputy Chief Officer for Project Delivery. Coordinates the work of multiple highly experienced subject matter experts across agency divisions and investigates/troubleshoots complex and sensitive issues relative to transportation project delivery.

Serves as a spokesperson for the portfolio of projects in communication with stakeholders within the agency, with other District agencies and the Executive Office of the Mayor, with Councilmembers and Advisory Neighborhood Commissions, with other project stakeholders (such as developers, utility companies, and federal agencies), and the general public. Provides reports, memorandums, and assessments for day-to-day project tracking of milestones and progress notes. This includes developing and planning key performance indicators and programs that are present to agency executives and other senior leadership throughout the District.

Qualification and Education

Degree:
Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor’s degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics.

Bachelor’s degree in urban planning, Engineering, or Public Administration preferred.

Or

Combination of education and experience
-- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering.

Specialized Experience:
Experience that equipped the applicant with the particular knowledge, skills and abilities to perform successfully the duties of the position, and the is typically in or related to the work of the position to be filled. To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the next lower grade level in the normal line of progression.

Licenses and Certification

Must possess and maintain a valid driver’s license

Working Conditions/Environment

The work is partially performed in an office setting which is adequately heated, ventilated, and lit. Frequently, the work will include filed visits to construction sites and other project sites where the incumbent is exposed to dust, chemical odors, construction hazards and variety weather conditions.

While at construction sites the incumbent is required to wear a hard hat and other protective equipment. Additionally, while at construction sites, there is a need to use caution to avoid the movement of building supplies, workpeople on ladders, mechanized equipment, slippery surfaces, etc.

, pursuant to section 410 Chapter 4 of the D.C. Personnel Regulations. Accordingly, the incumbent will be subject to pre-employment checks (criminal background checks, consumer credit check, traffic record checks, if applicable) as a condition of employment, and will be subject to periodic criminal background checks for the duration of your tenure.

employee position under the provisions of District Personnel Manual, Chapter 12.  As such, your services may be required in emergency situations to perform crucial duties, i.e., snow removal, debris removal, transportation, shelter operations, food distribution, and communication. These duties may be performed when the government is closed or when most employees are dismissed early.

This position is located in the Department of General Services, Capital Construction Division. DGS manages the capital improvement and construction program for District government facilities; real property for District government use; management of space in buildings operated or leased by District government for selling and leasing other District real property; and for providing building services for facilities owned or operated by the District. The Capital Construction Division implements and oversees the Capital Improvement Program for agencies within the District of Columbia, as well as executes the capital budget program, consisting of the rehabilitation of existing real property facilities, and construction of new facilities supporting the District. We are hiring for Project Managers within the Schools, Government Centers, Parks & Recreation and Special Projects portfolios.

planning, analysis, technical assistance and guidance for major actions, as well as program analysis of real estate project management and capital construction delivery activities in the District of Columbia. jobs.title: Data Center Project Manager, Critical Projects Implementation
jobs.description:
Description

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

The Critical Projects Implementation (CPI) team is a project management and execution team that manages construction activity within the operational data center spaces. The CPI team is tasked with critical infrastructure improvement projects to optimize utilization of space, power, and cooling within operational data centers around the globe. These activities are outside of the scope of standard construction delivery and regular preventative maintenance tasks.

We are currently seeking a Data Center Project Manager to serve as a technical resource within Amazon data centers. You will be part of a highly creative, efficient team tasked with tackling the most fascinating and challenges in designing, building, and operating Amazon data center facilities. The Project Manager is ultimately responsible for project oversight and review of all disciplines including electrical, mechanical, controls, and architectural. A fundamental understanding of these systems is required, as the individual will be expected to identify areas for improvement as well as act on data provided from other team and organizations. Ideal candidates will possess the ability to design, develop and deploy innovative solutions to address operational challenges. This role requires both independent contribution as well as the ability to work within multi-disciplinary teams. The scope of projects will include but not limited to the improvement of electrical, mechanical, fire detection and building automation system. The Project Manager is responsible for the overall direction, coordination, implementation, execution, control and completion of specific projects ensuring consistency with company strategy, commitments and goals.

About The Team

Why AWS

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of construction or project management experience
3+ years of vendor management experience
3+ years experience managing projects in data centers or comparable critical infrastructure in an operational space. Comparable critical infrastructure experience is defined as a facility that includes a 24/7 emergency backup system, manufacturing facility (semiconductor, auto, medical equipment or Clean rooms), Mass Transportation (freight or passenger rail), Oil and Gas, Utility, Hospitals or similar industry.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in engineering, project management, construction management or similar technical focus
3+ years of electrical or mechanical, or 3+ years of data center engineering experience
Experience managing projects in a fast pace environment
Demonstrated ability to understand and discuss technical concepts, manage trade-offs, incorporate feedback, and evaluate opportunistic new ideas with a variety of internal and external stakeholders

Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

The base salary range for this position is listed below. Your Amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. Learn more about our benefits at https://amazon.jobs/en/benefits.

jobs.description:
Department: Group HR – Baar

We are seeking a highly motivated Project Manager to join our Group Human Resources team. This role is ideal for someone who can think strategically to scope and plan projects, while also being hands-on and collaborating with others to develop solutions and following through to deliver outcomes.

Main tasks and responsibilities include:

Build strong relationships with Human Resources and business stakeholders and collaborate closely to align on priorities and deliver project outcomes.
Conduct data gathering and analysis to shape insights for projects and Group HR reporting to support stakeholder engagement and inform decision-making.
Develop and maintain the approach, tools and guidance for core talent processes (e.g., talent reviews, succession, organisation design, performance management).
Coordinate delivery of core talent processes such as performance management and succession planning.
Develop project plans, monitor progress, and ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget, and in line with target outcomes.
Prepare high-quality presentations and reports to effectively communicate findings, options, and key messages to stakeholders.
Support continuous improvement, identifying opportunities to optimise processes, tools, and ways of working to enhance efficiency and impact.
Facilitate working sessions, and stakeholder alignment meetings to ensure engagement and buy-in.
Support HR program governance, including reporting cadences, steering committee coordination, and decision-making protocols to ensure transparency and accountability across HR initiatives.
Manage project risks and issues proactively, escalating where appropriate and developing mitigation strategies.
Stay informed on industry trends and best practices, incorporating relevant insights into project recommendations.
Connect the dots across the projects you manage, stepping back to identify interdependencies and ensure activities are creating value for Glencore.
Support change management activities, including communication planning and stakeholder engagement, to ensure smooth adoption of new initiatives.

Our ideal candidate is:

Overall, a willingness and curiosity to expand your knowledge and take on new challenges in a fast-paced environment.
Strong communication skills and Spanish language skills are beneficial.
Analytical skills.
Attention to detail.
Synthesise complex information.
Stakeholder management and communication.
Project planning and prioritisation.
Strategic thinking and pragmatism.
Continuous improvement mindset.
Commitment to delivering high-quality outcomes.
Know-how of talent management and organisational development practices.
Proficiency with Excel, PowerPoint, and reporting/visualisation tools.

Qualifications and experience:

Degree or equivalent qualification in HR, Business Administration, or related field.
At least 5 years of experience in Management Consulting or Organisational Development; with a preference for Human Resources-related projects.
Collaborating with a broad range of HR and business stakeholders to scope and deliver project outcomes on time and in line with success criteria.
Designing and implementing global processes, frameworks, or approaches for Organisational Development topics (e.g., succession planning, performance management).
Demonstrated the ability to bring structure to complex and ambiguous problems, to understand the problem and root causes, and shape options and recommendations.
Applying advanced analytical skills to shape insights and findings from organisational data (e.g., structure, talent, survey, and succession data).
Keeping multiple projects on track, with clear visibility on progress, risks, and priorities.
Creating clear, compelling presentations and reports for senior stakeholder and governance forums conveying key findings, options, and messages in a way that builds understanding and buy-in.
Working in a complex global organisation, navigating multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.
Facilitating change management activities to support the successful implementation of talent and organisational development initiatives, ensuring sustainable behavioural and process change.

Benefits

We are committed to providing benefits, which promote mental, physical, and financial well-being. From healthy meal options in our restaurants and bistros to free use of the in-house gym including sport classes with professional trainers.
We reimburse public transport for commuting to work; alternatively, we offer free parking space.
We provide tuition assistance for further education and training courses.
We have a competitive parental leave policy. Our childcare benefits also include emergency childcare services and financial assistance towards daycare costs.
Employees’ Swiss Pension 2nd pillar is fully paid by Glencore.

Who We Are

Glencore is one of the world’s largest global diversified natural resource companies and a major producer and marketer of more than 60 commodities. Through a network of assets, customers and suppliers that spans the globe, we produce, process, recycle, source, market and distribute the commodities that advance everyday life.

With over 140,000 employees and contractors and a strong footprint in over 30 countries in both established and emerging regions for natural resources, our marketing and industrial activities are supported by a global network of offices.

Glencore’s customers are principally industrial consumers, such as those in the automotive, steel, power generation, battery manufacturing and oil sectors. We also provide financing, logistics and other services to producers and consumers of commodities.

jobs.title: Project Manager, Cost Control
jobs.description:
Summary

JOB DESCRIPTION

The Project Manager, Cost Control is responsible for planning, monitoring, and controlling project costs to ensure construction projects are delivered within approved budgets. The role involves cost forecasting, budget control, financial reporting, and coordination with project, commercial, and procurement teams to identify risks and improve cost efficiency throughout the project lifecycle.

Duties

Champions “The Layton Way” by delivering predictable outcomes for internal teams, external teams, and customers.
Ensures that “Constructing with Integrity” is delivered by working with honesty, unity, safety, and quality of work.
Develop and maintain the project budget, cost breakdown structure (CBS), and cost control procedures.
Monitor actual project costs against budgets and identify variances.
Determine whether entitlement exists for a change.
Prepare periodic cost reports, cash flow forecasts, and earned value analyses.
Review and validate subcontractor payment applications and progress claims.
Coordinate with planning/scheduling teams to align cost data with project schedules.
Track commitments, expenditures, and variations/change orders.
Analyze cost trends and recommend corrective actions to prevent cost overruns.
Support contract administration, including claims analysis and change management.
Participate in value engineering and cost optimization initiatives.
Ensure accurate cost records and documentation for audits and project close-out.
Provide cost advice to project management and senior leadership.
Assist in the preparation of final accounts and project financial closeout.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent experience.
Minimum 2 years of experience in cost control or project controls within the construction industry.
Proven experience in managing costs for large-scale construction projects (residential, commercial, industrial, or infrastructure).
Strong understanding of construction contracts (FIDIC or equivalent).
Strong understanding of all construction documents and how they interface.
Strong knowledge of cost control principles, budgeting, and financial forecasting.

Department Information
Are you interested in making a difference in the lives of fellow Californians while achieving your career goals? Do you set high standards for yourself and enjoy a collaborative and challenging work environment? The mission of the California Department of Social Services is to serve, protect, and support the people of California experiencing need in ways that empower wellbeing and disrupt systemic inequities. The vision of the California Department of Social Services is to provide quality services with a commitment to an inclusive, diverse, and equitable California where all people can thrive.

It is the mission of the Children's Residential Program to protect and improve the lives of all youth who reside in a community care facility through the administration of a transparent licensing system that is collaborative, fair, and supportive of families.

CDSS Guiding Principles

Diversity. Equity. Inclusion. Accessibility. Belonging.
We ensure opportunities for everyone to participate in a meaningful way in fulfilling the mission and vision of CDSS.

Community Engagement
We prioritize the lived experiences of community members as a driving force behind the creation, implementation, desired impact, or change of programs and services.

Empowerment
We engage, operate, and advocate from the understanding that each community and person have desires and capabilities to lead in their own life.

Quality Services
We provide services that align intent and impact by ensuring that they are accessible, community driven, interconnected, and continuously improved.

Data Defined Outcomes
We equitably collect and analyze data, take data-driven action, and measure outcomes relevant to those we serve, ensuring transparency and accountability.

Job Description And Duties
THE CALIFORNIA CHILDREN'S RESIDENTIAL PROGRAM WOODLANDS HILLS LOCAL UNIT IS RECRUITING FOR A LICENSING PROGRAM ANALYST (LPA). THIS POSITION IS LOCATED IN WOODLAND HILLS, CA.

Under the supervision of a Licensing Program Manager I (LPM I), the Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) is responsible for a full range of licensing duties which may include: developing and implementing orientations/training programs, reviewing applications, recommending license approval/denial, performing on-site facility evaluations, investigating complaints in licensed and unlicensed facilities, recommending and preparing administrative actions to deny, revoke, and suspend facility licenses.

Licensing Program Analysts (LPA) must possess a valid driver’s license and be able to travel frequently (sometimes overnight). LPAs must have good verbal and written communication skills and be able to maintain composure in stressful situations. LPAs are subject to fingerprinting and a criminal record check by the Department of Justice and Federal Bureau of Investigation.

The LPA will review and analyze special incident reports sent by providers to regional offices regarding the use of manual restraints and seclusions through Senate Bill (SB) 1043. SB 1043 creates the Accountability in Children’s Treatment Act, which enacts provisions related to incidents of seclusion or restraints of children in short-term residential therapeutic programs (STRTP) and requires the Department to increase transparency of actions STRTPs take when restraining a child and inform its emergency intervention policies to improve health and safety outcomes of children in out-of-home care. The LPA will review and prepare written summaries of incidents for publication and be part of the team that prepares and helps ensure the accuracy of the data published by the Department as required in SB 1043.

LPAs have regular contact with licensees, facility staff, children in care, their parents/responsible parties, and the public; may also meet with or conduct joint visits with fire marshals, long term care ombudsmen and other client advocates, local law enforcement and personnel from other agencies.

LPAs determine facility compliance or noncompliance with statutory and administrative law, issue civil penalties, and may be the first to detect and recommend the need for administrative or misdemeanor prosecution. Failure to observe and cite deficiencies may result in health and safety hazards to clients resulting in neglect, abuse, injury or death, and potential liability to the Department.

LPAs are supervised by a Licensing Program Manager I (LPM I). LPAs receive training and general instruction on licensing policy and division goals. LPMs closely supervise LPAs at Range A and B level and perform quality assurance evaluations frequently. As the level of expertise increases, the quality assurance evaluations are less frequent.

Projects / Industries: 
Life Sciences, R&D, Laboratories, Clean Rooms, Biotech, Pharma Manufacturing, etc.

Base salary: 130k - 200k DOE 

This is not an IT Project Manager role! Must-have prior experience in design engineering and construction firms. 
We are a globally recognized Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) firm delivering innovative solutions for some of the world's most technically complex and highly regulated facilities. Our teams partner with leading pharmaceutical, biotechnology, food and beverage, and advanced manufacturing organizations to design and deliver facilities that improve lives, enable innovation, and support operational excellence.
Our integrated approach combines engineering expertise, process knowledge, and project delivery excellence to create world-class manufacturing environments that are safe, sustainable, and efficient.

Position Overview

Senior Project Manager responsible for leading complex capital projects from concept through handover within the life sciences, food and beverage, and pharmaceutical manufacturing sectors. The role combines design engineering and construction management services with strong client relationship management to deliver safe, compliant, on-time and on-budget facilities. 

Key Responsibilities

Lead end-to-end project delivery including planning, design, procurement, construction, commissioning and closeout for life sciences and pharma manufacturing facilities.
Develop and implement project execution plans, schedules and budgets; manage scope, valuation, cost control and change management to maintain project financial performance.
Coordinate and oversee design engineering activities across core disciplines (mechanical, electrical, industrial, chemical) and integrate with architecture, process and validation teams.
Provide construction management services on site: supervise contractors, enforce quality and safety standards, resolve construction issues and maintain progress reporting.
Manage client relationships and stakeholder communications; provide regular status updates, negotiate scope and commercial terms, and ensure client requirements are fully met.
Identify, assess and mitigate project risks and technical complexities; lead problem solving and escalation processes to minimize impacts to schedule and cost.
Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and industry standards (GMP, FDA/EMA expectations, local building and safety codes) and support commissioning/validation activities.
Mentor and lead multidisciplinary project teams, consultants and subcontractors; promote continuous improvement and knowledge sharing across projects.
Oversee procurement strategy and vendor management to secure equipment, materials and services that meet technical and schedule requirements.
Prepare and present executive summaries, forecasts and technical reports for senior management and stakeholders.

Qualifications

Bachelors degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or related field; advanced degree preferred.
Minimum 7+ years of progressive project management experience delivering capital projects in life sciences, pharmaceutical manufacturing or AEC sectors, with demonstrated success on complex, high value programs.
Proven experience in design engineering oversight and construction management services across mechanical, electrical, industrial and/or chemical disciplines.
Strong understanding of pharma manufacturing processes, GMP requirements, commissioning and validation practices.
Demonstrated expertise in scope definition, valuation, complexity management, cost control and scheduling on multidiscipline projects.
Exceptional client relationship management skills with experience negotiating scope and commercial terms and maintaining senior stakeholder alignment.
Professional Project Management certification or equivalent is highly desirable.
Proficiency with project controls and collaboration tools (Primavera P6/MS Project, BIM software, cost control systems, MS Office).
Excellent leadership, communication and interpersonal skills; ability to lead multidisciplinary teams and make decisive technical and commercial decisions.

Minimum qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in a Life Science (e.g., Computational Biology, Chemistry), Physical Science (e.g., Physics, Materials Science), Mathematics, or Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience.
5 years of experience with technical programs, research engineering, or applied AI/ML projects (or 3 years with a PhD).

Preferred qualifications:

Experience analyzing model reasoning traces on graduate-level science problems, spotting flawed assumptions or hallucinations, and translating fixes into the training pipeline.
Experience designing lightweight, high-leverage systems for fast-moving empirical research; comfortable writing quick scripts or digging directly into datasets.
Knowledge of SFT data quality, RL reward signals, verifier calibration, and capability tradeoffs across model sizes.
Ability to audit individual tasks and rubrics beyond benchmark metrics.
Ability to thrive in ambiguous, high-velocity research environments; fluent in LLMs, SFT, RL, agentic evaluations, and Python-based scientific computing stacks.

About The Job

Google's projects, like our users, span the globe and require managers to keep the big picture in focus while being able to dive into the unique engineering challenges we face daily. As a Technical Program Manager at Google, you lead complex, multi-disciplinary engineering projects using your engineering expertise. You plan requirements with internal customers and usher projects through the entire project lifecycle. This includes managing project schedules, identifying risks and clearly communicating them to project stakeholders. You're equally at home explaining your team's analyses and recommendations to executives as you are discussing the technical trade-offs in product development with engineers.

Using your extensive technical and leadership expertise, you manage projects of various size and scope, identifying future opportunities, improving processes and driving the technical directions of your programs.

As a Technical Program Manager for Science & Reasoning, you will sit at the intersection of frontier AI model development and rigorous scientific domains across the life and physical sciences.

You will be in the technical weeds of model development — auditing scientific benchmarks, inspecting model reasoning trajectories and computational workflows, stress-testing RL verifiers, and shaping data and training priorities alongside research scientists and engineers.

You will drive stellar execution for our Science & Reasoning workstreams: turning research hypotheses into high-signal training data, verifiable RL environments, frontier evaluations, and deliverable model milestones across Gemini releases.

Artificial intelligence will be one of humanity’s most transformative inventions. At Google DeepMind, we are a pioneering AI lab with exceptional interdisciplinary teams focused on advancing AI development to solve complex global challenges and accelerate high-quality product innovation for billions of users. We use our technologies for widespread public benefit and scientific discovery, ensuring safety and ethics are always our highest priority.

We are pushing the boundaries across multiple domains. Our global teams offer diverse learning opportunities and varied career pathways for those driven to achieve exceptional results through collective effort.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $192000 - $278000 (USD) + 0% bonus target

Responsibilities

Learn more about benefits at Google .

Partner with research leads in life/physical sciences and formal reasoning to translate hypotheses into structured roadmaps, data mixtures, and Gemini release milestones.
Drive end-to-end execution for human data collection, synthetic data generation, SFT, and verifiable RL training environments like computational tool-use and code execution.
Curate and audit the evaluation suite for scientific reasoning and agentic workflows, ensuring benchmarks measure real-world scientific validity.
Work with post-training and RL leads to analyze checkpoints, inspect reasoning traces, identify capability gaps, and translate findings into immediate training interventions.
Manage cross-functional dependencies across data infrastructure, evaluation platforms, compute allocations, and external domain-expert vendors. Synthesize training dynamics and bottlenecks into clear launch criteria and actionable updates for tech leads.
