What You Will Do

Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) is seeking Project Manager 4 for the Project Analytics Division to lead cross-functional Integrated Project Teams (IPTs) in delivering complex projects. You will ensure project objectives meet the Project Owner's requirements while maintaining safety, quality, compliance, and cost and schedule commitments.

As a senior project manager, you will apply broad expertise to resolve complex challenges, develop effective project management approaches, and coordinate work across Laboratory organizations.

This position receives operational and functional direction from the Division Manager and provides technical and operational directions to assigned and deployed staff.

Key responsibilities include:

Maintains relationship with customers and stakeholders to understand and be responsive to their issues or concerns and works close with the project team and Information & Technology (I&T) staff regarding delivery of specific products and projects.
Applies Agile project management practices when appropriate (ensure the team is fully functional and productive, enable close corporation across all roles and functions, remove barriers and impediments that are preventing the team from completing work, shield the team from external interference, ensure the team follows their process and purses continuous innovation in their practices).
Knowledge of software development methodologies, tools and processes, including software development methodology framework source code control, application development tools and techniques, database design, development and management, programming languages, and component integration.
Manage assigned and deployed project personnel, coordinate assignments, and establish staffing needs based on current and projected workloads.
Provide personnel management for direct reports and direction to project staff, including construction, engineering, subcontractor oversight, project controls, quality, safety, and financial personnel.
Prepare, review, and present project progress reports, performance trends, risks, and recovery plans to management, customers, and federal sponsors, as applicable.
Maintain required safety and security training, integrate safety and security into every task, and stop work when continuing would be unsafe or compromise security.
Support a respectful and inclusive workplace free from discrimination and harassment.

What You Need

Minimum Job Requirements

Project Management:
Thorough knowledge of project management tools and techniques, with demonstrated experience managing major, complex projects involving multiple organizations. Ability to manage scope, budgets, schedules, resources, and performance and implement effective corrective actions.

Technical Knowledge:
Demonstrated knowledge of engineering, procurement, construction operations, construction technologies, and job site management, including their interfaces and inter-dependencies. Broad knowledge of applicable industry standards.

Leadership and Resource Management:
Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary teams, direct assigned and deployed staff, coordinate workloads, resolve conflicts, and manage competing priorities.

Customer and Stakeholder Engagement:
Ability to establish effective customer relationships and communicate project requirements, performance, and issues clearly to staff, management, and external stakeholders.

Control Account Management, When Assigned:
Subject matter expertise and proven experience in project controls or project management, including cost estimating, budgeting, cost control and analysis, scheduling, variance analysis, corrective actions, and accurate status reporting. Expert knowledge of Earned Value Management System (EVMS) tools and processes and sufficient engineering expertise to manage and monitor technical work.

Education

Position requires a bachelor's degree in project management, engineering, construction, business, or related field from an accredited institution and 12 years of directly related experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience directly related to the occupation.

Work Schedule:
Onsite / Hybrid: This position is located in Los Alamos, NM with the potential for a hybrid work arrangement (partially onsite/partially offsite) from a location within 2 hours ground commute of this location. Reporting onsite will be regularly required. Hybrid is at the discretion of management and can change at any time with appropriate notice

Position commitment:
Regular appointment employees are required to serve a period of continuous service in their current position in order to be eligible to apply for posted jobs throughout the Laboratory. If an employee has not served the time required, they may only apply for Laboratory jobs with the documented approval of their Division Leader. The position commitment for this position is 2 years.

Due to federal restrictions contained in the current National Defense Authorization Act, citizens of the People's Republic of China-including the special administrative regions of Hong Kong and Macau-as well as citizens of the Islamic Republic of Iran, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea), and the Russian Federation, who are not Lawful Permanent Residents ("green card" holders) are prohibited from accessing facilities that support the mission, functions, and operations of national security laboratories and nuclear weapons production facilities, which includes Los Alamos National Laboratory.

Located in beautiful northern New Mexico, Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) is a multidisciplinary research institution engaged in strategic science on behalf of national security. Our generous benefits package includes:

PPO or High Deductible medical insurance with the same large nationwide network

Design customized partner benefits and tailored value propositions that align with diverse partner business models, ensuring partners clearly recognize and capture measurable value from the program.

Collaborate with Product and Global Services teams to translate complex technical roadmaps into structured partner enablement and delivery frameworks.

Drive partner adoption and delivery readiness across critical technology pillars, including software-defined storage, container orchestration (Kubernetes), and advanced cloud security components.

Translate complex programmatic rules and technical solutions into compelling, easy-to-digest business narratives.

Manage and untangle complex customer entitlement frameworks with a focus on our commercial segment, ensuring partners can seamlessly navigate licensing, deployment rights, and service credits to accelerate time-to-value.
Data Analytics, Third-Party Tools & Operational Execution
Establish, monitor, and report on key performance indicators (KPIs) and operational metrics to evaluate global program health, partner performance, and ROI.
Provide thought leadership to internal executive teams and external partner leaders, presenting clear, data-driven programmatic strategies.
Navigate and influence a high-energy corporate culture with diverse, strong personalities by building consensus and driving alignment across regional and global teams.
Leverage and navigate diverse third-party tools and enterprise platforms to extract, analyze, and synthesize raw data outputs into structured, highly actionable operational execution plans.
Cross-Functional Collaboration, Advisory Boards & Events
Partner closely with Pre-Sales and Professional Services Organizations (PSO) to establish, cultivate, and lead global Services Advisory Boards, capturing partner feedback to influence long-term corporate strategy.
Drive thought leadership and end-to-end execution of services engagement events globally, positioning our organization as a premier services enablement engine for partners.
Act as the strategic bridge between technical pre-sales engineering, field delivery teams, marketing and partner ecosystems to ensure cohesive global messaging and programmatic alignment.

Education: Required to hold both a Bachelor’s degree (in Business, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field) AND or a Master’s degree (MBA or Master of Science in a relevant discipline).
Experience: Minimum of 15 years of progressive industry experience within the enterprise software, cloud infrastructure, or technology sector, with a definitive focus on Channel Program Management and Professional Services.
Tools & Analytical Skills: Advanced data literacy with a proven ability to work with third-party applications/tools and extract raw metrics to drive strategic program execution. Strong proficiency in building executive-level reports, dashboards, and consumption metrics.
VMware Domain Expertise: Strong working knowledge of VMware technologies, specifically the VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) platform architecture and its component stacks (including vSAN/Storage, Tanzu/Kubernetes, and NSX/Security).
Program & Business Acumen: Direct experience structuring partner certification requirements, managing global routes to market, and operationalizing customer entitlement models. Experience with AI models and output preferred.
Global Scale: Proven track record of managing programs across multiple geographies (AMER, EMEA, APJ) while accounting for regional market nuances.

Innovative & "Outside-the-Box" Thinking: Proven ability to look past legacy programmatic frameworks to design non-traditional workflows, creative incentive structures, and novel problem-solving methodologies. You don't just manage existing programs; you re-imagine them to solve complex global channel friction.
High Emotional Intelligence (EQ): Proven ability to challenge the status quo, handle strong personalities, and command respect through competence and diplomatic communication.
Communication Excellence: Exceptional written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to distill highly technical concepts or dense programmatic data into clear business value for executive-level audiences.

Description Of Job

The Assistant Project Manager supports the successful planning, coordination, and delivery of projects, helping to ensure they achieve agreed objectives, timescales, budgets, and quality requirements. Working closely with the Project Manager and wider project team, the role provides coordination, reporting, governance, stakeholder engagement, and project control support throughout the project lifecycle.

The Assistant Project Manager acts as a key point of communication between project stakeholders, suppliers, and delivery teams, assisting with the management of schedules, risks, issues, actions, costs, and project documentation. The role supports effective decision-making and contributes to the successful delivery of projects in accordance with organisational standards and project management processes.

Key Responsibilities

Support the delivery of projects across all lifecycle phases, including definition, design, procurement, manufacture, construction, and commissioning.
Assist the Project Manager in monitoring project performance against scope, schedule, cost, quality, and delivery objectives.
Support the management of project scope and the administration of change control processes.
Coordinate project activities to ensure delivery milestones and objectives are achieved.
Support mobilisation of project teams and coordination of project start-up activities.
Assist in the development, maintenance, and communication of Project Management Plans, schedules, and governance arrangements.
Coordinate stakeholder engagement activities and support project readiness reviews.
Support the development and maintenance of project schedules, budgets, and forecasts.
Assist in maintaining Work Breakdown Structures (WBS), Cost Breakdown Structures (CBS), and organisational reporting structures.
Collect, analyse, and report project performance data to support effective project controls.
Assist with cost tracking, commitment management, and cost-to-complete forecasting.
Support procurement activities, including preparation of enquiry documentation and supplier engagement.
Assist with tender evaluations and supplier assessments.
Monitor supplier and subcontractor performance and support contract administration activities.
Ensure procurement records and documentation are maintained accurately.
Produce project reports, dashboards, and management information for internal and external stakeholders.
Coordinate project review meetings and maintain actions, decisions, and project records.
Monitor project progress and highlight potential issues, risks, or variances to the Project Manager.
Support governance processes and maintain compliance with project management procedures.

Qualifications, Experience And Skills

Qualification in Engineering, Project Management, Business Management, or a related discipline.
Working towards or holding a recognised project management qualification (e.g., APM PMQ, PRINCE2 Practitioner, PMP or equivalent).
Demonstrates professional standards of behaviour and compliance with legal, regulatory, and technical requirements.
Good commercial awareness and understanding of project financial management principles.
Experience within a project, engineering, construction, or programme delivery environment.
Demonstrable experience supporting project delivery, project controls, planning, project engineering, or project coordination activities.
Good organisational, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Developing problem-solving, planning, and risk management skills.
Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.
Full UK driving licence.

ILIOS Overview

ILIOS is the Construction Partner for the UK’s STEP (Spherical Tokamak for Energy Production) fusion programme, the UK’s world‑leading programme to design and build a prototype fusion energy power plant at West Burton in Nottinghamshire.

ILIOS is a consortium led by a joint venture between Kier and Nuvia, supported by AECOM, AL_A and Turner & Townsend, bringing together extensive experience across major national infrastructure, nuclear and safety‑critical engineering, complex site transformation, programme and cost management, and world‑class design.

Working as part of the public–private sector integrated team led by UK Fusion Energy (UKFE), a wholly owned subsidiary of the UK Atomic Energy Authority (UKAEA), ILIOS is embedded in the programme as STEP transitions from planning into delivery.

The consortium supports the design and construction of buildings, infrastructure and facilities across the STEP site, alongside constructability, programme planning, site management, supply‑chain engagement and project controls, helping to ensure delivery is safe, buildable and fully integrated with the wider programme.

The appointment of ILIOS marks a significant milestone in the UK’s transition to clean energy and supports STEP’s mission to demonstrate fusion energy and develop a world‑leading fusion supply chain, creating long‑term economic and skills opportunities for the UK.

new_jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an ERM Program Manager based in Canada.

We are seeking an experienced Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) professional to oversee the execution and continuous improvement of risk management operations within a fast-growing, regulated financial services environment. In this hands-on role, you will coordinate risk assessments, maintain enterprise risk registers, and ensure that risk information is accurate, consistent, and actionable. You will collaborate with stakeholders across Legal, Compliance, Finance, Product, Security, and Operations to identify emerging risks and drive effective mitigation plans. You will also develop key risk indicators, validate risk assessments with functional owners, and prepare executive-level and board-ready reporting. Working within an established ERM framework, you will help strengthen risk visibility, accountability, and governance across multiple entities and jurisdictions. This remote opportunity is ideal for a detail-oriented professional who combines strong risk management expertise with excellent communication skills and the ability to influence stakeholders without direct authority.

Accountabilities

Enterprise Risk Management Execution: Manage the end-to-end ERM intake process, collecting risk information through tickets, functional interviews, surveys, incident reports, and operational channels.
Risk Register Management: Maintain functional and enterprise risk registers within the designated Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) platform, ensuring accurate documentation of risk owners, inherent and residual scores, mitigation measures, and status updates.
Risk Assessment and Scoring: Apply the established ERM risk scoring model, work with risk owners to validate residual risk ratings, and ensure consistent assessment practices across business functions.
Risk Taxonomy and Classification: Map identified risks to established Level 1 and Level 2 risk categories and relevant enterprise risk scenarios to support consistent classification, analysis, and reporting.
Stakeholder Coordination: Organize regular check-ins with functional risk leads, follow up on outstanding actions and blockers, consolidate inputs, and ensure alignment between functional and enterprise-level risk assessments.
Mitigation Planning and Escalation: Track risk mitigation plans, action owners, target completion dates, and progress. Escalate overdue actions, unresolved issues, and significant risk exposures to the appropriate stakeholders.
Key Risk Indicators (KRIs): Collaborate with data owners to define and monitor relevant KRIs, using appropriate proxy metrics where data collection or measurement capabilities are still developing.
Executive and Board Reporting: Prepare clear, accurate, and decision-oriented ERM reports, executive summaries, risk dashboards, and board materials that communicate the organization's risk exposure and mitigation progress.
ERM Governance and Coordination: Support ERM Working Group meetings by preparing agendas, documenting minutes, tracking decisions, and following up on assigned actions.
Risk Intake Triage: Operate the risk intake workflow by evaluating and scoring incoming items, identifying duplicates, and recording relevant risks and follow-up actions in the appropriate systems.
Process Documentation and Enablement: Develop practical playbooks, templates, and guidance materials to help functional risk leads apply consistent risk identification, assessment, and reporting practices.
Entity-Level Risk Management: Coordinate quarterly risk updates across local entities, ensuring timely submissions, consistent reporting, and appropriate escalation of significant issues.
Emerging Risk Monitoring: Identify and surface emerging risks related to cryptocurrency, artificial intelligence, regulatory developments, and multi-jurisdictional operations for further assessment and review.

Requirements

Professional Experience: Approximately 5–10 years of experience in operational risk, Enterprise Risk Management (ERM), Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC), or compliance program management within a regulated financial institution, fintech, broker-dealer, or capital markets environment.
Hands-On ERM Execution: Demonstrated experience managing risk registers from initial intake and assessment through mitigation tracking and executive reporting. Practical operational experience is essential, beyond framework design alone.
Risk Assessment Expertise: Strong understanding of risk identification, inherent and residual risk scoring, mitigation planning, risk ownership, and ongoing monitoring.
GRC Platforms: Practical experience using GRC platforms to manage risk registers, workflows, controls, assessments, and reporting.
Stakeholder Management: Proven ability to coordinate and influence cross-functional stakeholders across Legal, Compliance, Finance, Product, Security, and Operations without relying on direct reporting authority.
Regulatory Knowledge: Familiarity with SEC and FINRA requirements, or equivalent experience operating within a regulated financial services environment.
Reporting and Communication: Excellent written communication skills, with the ability to develop clear risk statements, executive summaries, structured risk tables, and board-ready materials.
Risk Governance and Metrics: Experience tracking mitigation actions, monitoring operational risk indicators, defining KRIs, and escalating issues according to established governance processes.
Analytical and Organizational Skills: Strong attention to detail, sound judgment, and the ability to consolidate complex information from multiple sources into actionable insights.
Autonomy and Accountability: A proactive, hands-on approach to program execution, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, maintain accurate documentation, and deliver reporting within established deadlines.
Preferred Financial Services Experience: Exposure to broker-dealer, clearing, or custody operations, particularly in environments with complex operational and regulatory requirements.
Preferred Fintech Experience: Experience implementing or operating ERM programs within a high-growth fintech or financial services organization.
Preferred Digital Asset Risk Knowledge: Familiarity with cryptocurrency or digital asset risk management and associated operational considerations.
Preferred Multi-Entity Experience: Experience consolidating risk information across multiple legal entities, business units, or jurisdictions.
Preferred Workflow and Framework Knowledge: Familiarity with Jira Service Management, structured risk intake workflows, COSO ERM, or ISO 31000, particularly from an operational implementation perspective.
Preferred Board Reporting Experience: Previous experience preparing materials for board meetings, risk committees, or senior leadership governance forums.
Location and Work Arrangement: Based in Canada, with the ability to work remotely within the applicable hiring and employment arrangements.

Stock options, offering the opportunity to participate in the company's long-term growth.
Health benefits.
One-time home-office setup allowance of USD $500 for new hires.
Monthly stipend of USD $150, provided through a Brex card, to support eligible work-related expenses.

By normalizing health & wellness challenges and innovating on their solutions, we’re making better health outcomes easier to achieve.

Hims & Hers is a public company, traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol “HIMS.” To learn more about the brand and offerings, you can visit hims.com/about and hims.com/how-it-works . For information on the company’s outstanding benefits, culture, and its talent-first flexible/remote work approach, see below and visit www.hims.com/careers-professionals.

About The Role

This is a rare opportunity to help define a function and leave a fingerprint on how global healthcare packaging gets made. As our Principal Design Program Manager for International Packaging and Industrial Design, you won't just run programs; you'll establish the philosophy, frameworks, and standards that future DPMs will build on.

You'll be handed ambiguous, high-stakes problems and expected to bring structure, strategy, and a point of view in addition to consistent and quality execution. Your decisions will shape how design, marketing, supply chain, and operations work together at a systems level across three global markets.

We're building a design operations function that believes process and operations is a creative act, and that the best systems make great design possible. If you thrive in ambiguity, build with intention, and know how to make global design and packaging programs run, we'd love to talk.

You Will

STRATEGIC IMPACT & ORGANIZATIONAL INFLUENCE

Define What Great Looks Like

Establish the standard for how design operates globally: the frameworks, decision-making models, and principles you build become the foundation the team scales from.
Operate as the internal subject matter authority on global packaging program management. Leadership, design, legal, and supply chain turn to you for strategic counsel and guidance.
Contribute to process development, onboarding standards, and the craft development of the DPM function as it grows.
Build the frameworks other DPMs and future hires will use, this is as much about designing the operating system as running it.

Drive org-level prioritization

Design the global prioritization framework, the criteria, inputs, and escalation model that surface regional urgency, regulatory deadlines, creative capacity, and business impact, so that decision-makers can make faster, better-informed tradeoff calls.
Build the mechanisms (dashboards, briefing formats, escalation paths) that get the right tradeoffs in front of the right leaders before they become problems.
Influence roadmap and planning decisions across design, supply chain, and marketing by providing a clear, data-informed picture of capacity and risk.

PROGRAM EXECUTION & REGIONAL OWNERSHIP

Global program leadership

Architect and steer the end-to-end program model for packaging and print graphics across multiple regions, including AU, CAN, and UK, in close partnership with regional design and production teams. You are the connective tissue ensuring timeline integrity, dependency mapping, and risk visibility, not the sole executor of regional work.
Build and maintain strong regional relationships with design, marketing, supply chain, and legal counterparts in each market, trusted enough that people come to you early.

Compliance & regulatory fluency

Develop working knowledge of healthcare packaging compliance requirements across regions, and embed compliance checkpoints upstream in the creative process.
Translate regulatory requirements into clear creative briefs and review criteria that designers and legal can both work from.

Creative partnership

Partner with designers from brief through final production file, understanding creative intent well enough to protect it through the operational and compliance gauntlet.
Bring broad fluency across print graphics production, structural packaging, and industrial design/CMF — color management, dielines, press-ready specs, vendor pre-press workflows — enough to translate between disciplines, ask the right questions, and know where things typically break. You're not expected to be the deepest expert in any one domain, but you're the person who can speak all their languages and engage credibly in each conversation.
Build the mechanisms — capacity dashboards, resourcing reviews, structured tradeoff conversations — that make the creative team's bandwidth and constraints visible to stakeholders, so capacity conversations happen proactively with leadership rather than reactively with designers.

You Have

8-10+ years in design program management or creative operations, with meaningful time in healthcare, consumer goods, or a regulated packaging environment.
Proven track record building processes from scratch. You've created process infrastructure where little existed, and you're energized by that, not intimidated by it.
Broad packaging program expertise. You've owned programs from kickoff to press check and can speak to exactly where things typically go wrong to avoid it.
Demonstrated organizational influence. You've shaped how a team or function operates beyond your own programs, without relying on leadership to do it.
Experience designing prioritization frameworks that stakeholders actually adopt — not just building Gantt charts, but shifting how an org makes sequencing decisions.
Cross-disciplinary fluency in industrial design, structural packaging, and CMF — enough to be a credible partner across the full packaging design ecosystem, without needing to be the deepest expert in any one area.
Proficiency with PM tooling (Asana, Airtable, Google Suite, Dropbox) and comfort reviewing work in Figma.

Unlimited PTO, company holidays, and quarterly mental health days
Comprehensive health benefits including medical, dental & vision, and parental leave

Description

Amazon's Global Standards & Customer Excellence (GSCE) organization owns the Worldwide Scorecard - the mechanism that provides a holistic view of operational performance across Safety, People, Customer Experience, Quality, Cost, and Sustainability pillars for 1,000+ last-mile delivery stations and sort centers spanning North America, Europe, Japan, India, and ECCF. The WW Benchmarking team within GSCE manages performance benchmarking using the Continuous Benchmarking Rate Setting (CBRS) methodology - clustering stations into peer groups and setting statistically rigorous performance targets that control for non-ops factors.

As the Senior Program Manager for the Quality Pillar, you will own end-to-end benchmarking and scorecard strategy for First Pass Yield (FPY), Stow Buffer Compliance, and emerging quality metrics across all regions. You will drive the CBRS methodology for quality KPIs, launch and scale benchmarking studies that close performance gaps at underperforming stations, develop next-generation metrics that replace legacy measurements, and feed input-level KPIs into the Risk Engine that powers predictive operational alerts. You will partner with Operations, ACES, BIE (Analytics), and Finance teams to ensure quality benchmarks are accurate, equitable, and drive measurable operational improvement across stations worldwide.

This role requires strong analytical thinking, program management rigor, and the ability to translate complex statistical methodologies into operator-friendly insights. You will manage multiple concurrent workstreams - from quarterly benchmark refreshes, to multi-month benchmarking studies with site-level interventions, to expanding quality benchmarks to new regions and business units where none previously existed. You will also build AI-powered tooling that accelerates validation and delivery, and contribute input signals to the Gravion Risk Engine. Cross-team coordination, data fluency, stakeholder communication to senior leadership, and a bias for automation are essential.

You will be a strong partner of Central and Field ACES teams - delivering operator sentiment of the metrics, benchmarking the metrics and aligning closely with their OP process, initiating metric changes, and maintaining metric parity around the world.

Key job responsibilities

Own the Quality Pillar benchmarking portfolio end-to-end — vision, methodology, and cadence for FPY, Stow Buffer Compliance, and future quality metrics across NA, EU, JP, ECCF, RSR, and RoW
Drive benchmarking methodology for quality KPIs — quarterly benchmark generation, cluster design, sub-cluster coefficients, and statistical model improvement
Design benchmarking studies identifying root causes at underperforming stations, sharing best practices, and driving measurable quality improvement
Expand quality benchmarks to new regions and BUs — adapting methodology for local data, gaining alignment, and launching benchmarks where none existed
Own Road to CBRS (benchmarking) for quality metrics — translating benchmarks into actionable station-level insights that close the gap
Partner with Central and Field ACES on operator sentiment, OP alignment, and worldwide metric parity
Define upstream quality KPI signals for the Risk Engine — early-warning indicators and data integration partnership
Build AI-powered validation tooling — cluster analyzers, anomaly detection, and self-service analytics for operators
Partner with BIE on data pipeline requirements — freshness, accuracy, and scalability in Andes/Redshift
Present insights, study results, and methodology recommendations to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders
Write quality pillar narratives for quarterly publications and stakeholder newsletters

A day in the life

Monday: Review CBRS cluster refresh — identify sub-cluster movements, flag quality KPI anomalies, prep stakeholder insights. Tuesday: Triage Asana intakes, meet operators to answer benchmark and cluster placement questions.
Mid-week: Strategic alignment with stakeholders on metric logic, long-term vision, and network performance. Meet cross-BU stakeholders on benchmarking expansion needs for quality metrics.
Thursday: Deep methodology work — review site outliers per Quality Pillar KPI, discuss logic changes with regional stakeholders, assess network impact.
Friday: Document weekly quality benchmarking performance, update study progress, share best practices from top stations, field operator gap-closure questions.

new_jobs.title: Senior Program Manager II - Laser Communications
new_jobs.description:
About Rocket Lab

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we’re building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, laser communication terminals, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

SENIOR PROGRAM MANAGER II - LASER COMMUNICATIONS

Laser communication is the backbone of the constellations of today and tomorrow, and demand for it is growing fast. We are scaling industry-leading optical communication terminals to meet it: high-performing, affordable, and available at the volume commercial and government constellation operators need. Based at Rocket Lab’s global headquarters in Long Beach, CA, you are the customer’s champion and the delivery lead for our optical communication terminal programs. You own the customer outcome: the day-to-day relationship, delivery commitments and schedule at rate, milestone and acceptance reviews, risk, and program health. You build on a proven, standard terminal product and partner closely with our Product team on configuration, pricing, and new customer needs. You’ll work alongside the teams that build the spacecraft, the components, and the rockets, so the people you need to solve a problem are down the hall, not under another contract. This is a high-impact, customer-facing role: you connect the customer, our engineering teams, the production line, and the business across two continents, and you’re the person our customers count on.

What You’ll Get To Do

Lead Delivery: Lead terminal programs from award through qualification, production at rate, delivery, and on-orbit checkout, across current-generation production and next-generation variants. Hold each program to its plan and deliver on schedule, technical performance, and every customer commitment.
Lead the Team of Teams: Run multiple concurrent customer programs, work closely with Chief Engineers on link performance, data rate, SWaP, environmental qualification, and optical terminal interoperability, and dive in personally on the problems that matter most to delivery.
Deliver at Rate: Own each program’s delivery profile and protect it. Spot yield, supplier, and test-capacity risk early and drive it to closure with Operations and the Product team.
Forge the Supply Chain: Partner with Supply Chain to manage critical suppliers as strategic partners, building the relationships and accountability that keep every customer delivery on schedule.
Run the Program Lifecycle: Own program startup and baselining, milestone and qualification reviews, export and ITAR obligations with Trade Compliance, customer acceptance, and closeout across our U.S. and European sites.
Champion the Customer: Be the trusted point of contact for customers through milestone reviews, interoperability campaigns, acceptance, and delivery. Partner with BD & Strategy on proposals and with the Product team on pricing and configuration, bringing the voice of the customer to every decision.
Raise the Bar: Mentor the people around you, set a high standard for how we show up for customers, and help develop the program leaders who will run our next generation of laser communications programs.

QUALIFICATIONS YOU’LL BRING AS A SENIOR PROGRAM MANAGER II

Engineering Foundation: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Physics, or Math.
Technical Depth: Working understanding of free-space optical or RF communications: link budgets, pointing, acquisition, and tracking, modems and coding, and space or airborne environmental qualification.
8+ years in space, aerospace, or photonics hardware programs, with multiple full program cycles. We weight the hardest thing you’ve shipped over the count.
Customer Delivery: A track record of leading a complex hardware program to delivery (customer, schedule, risk, and acceptance) and carrying it across the finish line under real pressure.
Production Delivery: Evidence you’ve moved real hardware from prototype to qualified, rate-production delivery to customers.
Program Financials: Experience managing program cost, EAC, and customer contract changes in partnership with finance and product teams on a program of meaningful scale.
Proof Point: You’ve delivered hardware at rate to a demanding customer and kept their trust through a hard moment, such as a slip, a test failure, or a contract change.
Clearance: U.S. Person status required (ITAR/EAR); ability to obtain a security clearance preferred.

These Qualifications Would Be Nice To Have

Domain Authority: Direct experience with optical inter-satellite links or optical ground or airborne terminals.
Production Velocity: A proven playbook for taking low-volume, hand-built optical or electro-optical hardware into high-rate production without sacrificing reliability.
Constellation Fluency: Experience delivering to large commercial or defense constellation programs.
Customer Leadership: Experience as the primary customer interface for constellation operators or satellite primes, from kickoff through acceptance.
Global Leadership: Experience leading program work across geographically dispersed sites, including export-control and dual-use compliance.
Advanced Technical Credibility: A Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Optics/Photonics, Physics, or a related field.
Systems & Toolchain Fluency: You speak systems engineering (trade studies, interface control, requirement integrity) and use Jira, Confluence, and ERP/MRP to keep program health visible at speed.
AI Fluency: You put AI tools to work in day-to-day program management, from schedule and risk analysis to status reporting and customer communications, so you and your team spend more time on the problems that matter.

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Anticipated annual equity grant value is designed around function, level, experience, and other factors; realized value depends on vesting and stock-price performance.Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Total Compensation (base and equity): $166,800 USD - $258,625 USD

Base Salary: $134,300 USD - $201,350 USD

What To Expect

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Important Information

Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

The Mid Level Process Control System Project Manager is responsible for managing projects for the Class I, II, and III control system modernization and upgrade program, as well as ancillary controls-related projects for Large Industries. The role currently focuses on managing Class II and III projects within the modernization program and ancillary sub-projects that support and accelerate key programs.

The Process Control Technology (PCT) projects portfolio covers Large Industries operations across North America.At Air Liquide we RESPECT, HONOR and VALUE diversity.

We are looking for you!

Comprehensive Family Benefits: Air Liquide offers a full benefits package designed to support your whole life, including Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, AD&D, and Disability Insurance.

Future Security: 401(k) Retirement Plan with company match, Tuition Assistance, Paid Holidays, Vacation, and Sick time.

Key Responsibilities:

Project Execution & Technical Management

Lead the estimating, planning, execution, and schedule/cost management of Class I, II, and III Distributed Control System (DCS) Upgrade projects, with budgets ranging from $250k to $8MM.

Create scope of work documents and lead the bid process to select 3rd party contractors.

Manage and direct 3rd party contractors for the successful execution of control system projects.

Actively coordinate and manage the Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) for all control system projects.

Liaise with the Engineering & Construction department to ensure control system projects are delivered to plants in accordance with specified standards.

Collaborate with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) to ensure control system designs adhere to all applicable standards and closely manage the incorporation of upgrade program standards.

Coordinate with multiple disciplines, including Corporate OT, Electrical, Plant Operations, and Instrumentation teams, to ensure comprehensive project coverage during upgrades.

Apply knowledge of National Electrical Code (NEC), OSHA, and ISA standards, along with a general understanding of the mechanical, electrical, instrumentation, and control systems utilized in Air Liquide technologies.

Read, interpret, and mark up Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs), and perform basic process calculations.

Project Management & Financial Control

Manage multiple projects concurrently, demonstrating proven competency in scoping, estimating, scheduling (critical path analysis), budgeting, cost control, and design/scope change management.

Develop comprehensive Project Statements of Work (SOWs) and prepare preliminary estimates for project funding requests.

Utilize project estimates and vendor quotes to establish project budgets (Pre-FEED and FEED studies).

Create and manage purchase orders and change orders using the Oracle system.

Maintain meticulous tracking of expenses against the budget, providing weekly financial updates to appropriate personnel.

Process Improvement & Strategic Sourcing

Support procurement efforts in securing beneficial frame agreements with key 3rd party suppliers.

Learn and assess existing engineering processes to identify and report deviations, while actively contributing to the definition and evolution of project management execution standards.

Collaborate with the Project Management department to evolve the role and provide project management assistance to Junior Engineers as required.

Continuously seek and implement improved strategies for managing projects and commit to continuous professional growth through formal and informal training.

Education & Certifications

Licensure: Professional Engineer (PE) registration is desirable.

Certification: Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification is required, or the candidate must be willing to obtain certification within 18 to 24 months of hire.

Experience

Minimum of 8 years of experience in control system project management or control systems engineering, encompassing full project lifecycle responsibilities.

Proven competency in managing projects utilizing industry-standard project management methodologies and tools.

new_jobs.title: Senior Field Project Manager
Senior Program Manager I - Laser Communications
new_jobs.description:
About Rocket Lab

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we’re building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, laser communication terminals, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

SENIOR PROGRAM MANAGER I - LASER COMMUNICATIONS

Laser communication is the backbone of the constellations of today and tomorrow, and demand for it is growing fast. We are scaling industry-leading optical communication terminals to meet it: high-performing, affordable, and available at the volume commercial and government constellation operators need. Based at Rocket Lab’s global headquarters in Long Beach, CA, you are the customer’s champion and the delivery lead for our optical communication terminal programs. You own the customer outcome: the day-to-day relationship, delivery commitments and schedule at rate, milestone and acceptance reviews, risk, and program health. You build on a proven, standard terminal product and partner closely with our Product team on configuration, pricing, and new customer needs. You’ll work alongside the teams that build the spacecraft, the components, and the rockets, so the people you need to solve a problem are down the hall, not under another contract. This is a high-impact, customer-facing role: you connect the customer, our engineering teams, the production line, and the business across two continents, and you’re the person our customers count on.

What You'll Get To Do

Lead Delivery: Lead terminal programs from award through qualification, production at rate, delivery, and on-orbit checkout, across current-generation production and next-generation variants. Hold each program to its plan and deliver on schedule, technical performance, and every customer commitment.
Lead the Team of Teams: Run multiple concurrent customer programs, work closely with Chief Engineers on link performance, data rate, SWaP, environmental qualification, and optical terminal interoperability, and dive in personally on the problems that matter most to delivery.
Deliver at Rate: Own each program’s delivery profile and protect it. Spot yield, supplier, and test-capacity risk early and drive it to closure with Operations and the Product team.
Forge the Supply Chain: Partner with Supply Chain to manage critical suppliers as strategic partners, building the relationships and accountability that keep every customer delivery on schedule.
Run the Program Lifecycle: Own program startup and baselining, milestone and qualification reviews, export and ITAR obligations with Trade Compliance, customer acceptance, and closeout across our U.S. and European sites.
Champion the Customer: Be the trusted point of contact for customers through milestone reviews, interoperability campaigns, acceptance, and delivery. Partner with BD & Strategy on proposals and with the Product team on pricing and configuration, bringing the voice of the customer to every decision.
Raise the Bar: Mentor the people around you, set a high standard for how we show up for customers, and help develop the program leaders who will run our next generation of laser communications programs.

You'll Bring These Qualifications As Senior Program Manager i

Engineering Foundation: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Physics, or Math.
Technical Depth: Working understanding of free-space optical or RF communications: link budgets, pointing, acquisition, and tracking, modems and coding, and space or airborne environmental qualification.
5+ years in space, aerospace, or photonics hardware programs, with multiple full program cycles. We weight the hardest thing you’ve shipped over the count.
Customer Delivery: A track record of leading a complex hardware program to delivery (customer, schedule, risk, and acceptance) and carrying it across the finish line under real pressure.
Production Delivery: Evidence you’ve moved real hardware from prototype to qualified, rate-production delivery to customers.
Program Financials: Experience managing program cost, EAC, and customer contract changes in partnership with finance and product teams on a program of meaningful scale.
Proof Point: You’ve delivered hardware at rate to a demanding customer and kept their trust through a hard moment, such as a slip, a test failure, or a contract change.
Clearance: U.S. Person status required (ITAR/EAR); ability to obtain a security clearance preferred.

These Qualifications Would Be Nice To Have

Domain Authority: Direct experience with optical inter-satellite links or optical ground or airborne terminals.
Production Velocity: A proven playbook for taking low-volume, hand-built optical or electro-optical hardware into high-rate production without sacrificing reliability.
Constellation Fluency: Experience delivering to large commercial or defense constellation programs.
Customer Leadership: Experience as the primary customer interface for constellation operators or satellite primes, from kickoff through acceptance.
Global Leadership: Experience leading program work across geographically dispersed sites, including export-control and dual-use compliance.
Advanced Technical Credibility: A Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Optics/Photonics, Physics, or a related field.
Systems & Toolchain Fluency: You speak systems engineering (trade studies, interface control, requirement integrity) and use Jira, Confluence, and ERP/MRP to keep program health visible at speed.
AI Fluency: You put AI tools to work in day-to-day program management, from schedule and risk analysis to status reporting and customer communications, so you and your team spend more time on the problems that matter.

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Anticipated annual equity grant value is designed around function, level, experience, and other factors; realized value depends on vesting and stock-price performance.Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Total Compensation (base and equity): $137,075 USD - $196,275 USD

Base Salary: $116,800 USD - $160,600 USD

What To Expect

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Important Information

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here.

Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com.This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY:

For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant. These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations.

Under these Regulations, you may be ineligible for this role if you do not hold citizenship of Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the European Union, or a country that is part of NATO, or if you hold ineligible dual citizenship or nationality. For more information on these Regulations, click here ITAR Regulations.

Comcast Business has been consistently recognized by industry analysts and associations as a leader and innovator, and one of the fastest growing providers of Ethernet services.

Job Summary

We are looking for an experienced Project Manager to lead end-to-end customer migration projects as organisations move from their existing service providers to Comcast Business solutions. Acting as the customer’s main delivery contact, you will coordinate complex, multi-site network migrations involving technologies such as SD-WAN (Fortinet and Cisco Meraki), MPLS, VPLS, broadband and 4G/5G connectivity. You will combine a strong understanding of telecommunications delivery with disciplined project management to achieve safe, predictable and high-quality outcomes for customers.

new_jobs.title: Space All-Source Intelligence Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Description

Are you passionate about using intelligence analysis to solve complex challenges in the space domain?

Do you enjoy turning intelligence from multiple sources into actionable data that can inform modeling, simulation, and analysis?

Are you interested in working alongside engineers, modelers, and analysts to help assess and forecast national security space threats?

If so, we're looking for someone like you to join our team at APL!

We are seeking a Space All-Source Intelligence Analyst to support programs within APL's National Security Space Mission Area (NSSMA). You will apply your knowledge of the Intelligence Community (IC) and experience with all-source intelligence analysis to help address critical challenges facing the Department of Defense (DoD) and Intelligence Community in the space domain.

In this role, you will serve as a critical link between intelligence and the technical teams developing high-fidelity modeling, simulation, and analysis (MS&A) capabilities. Rather than focusing primarily on traditional intelligence reporting, you will acquire, analyze, and translate intelligence from multiple classified sources into the quantitative data, parameters, and operational context needed to develop realistic models and simulations. You will collaborate closely with systems engineers, modelers, data scientists, and program teams to ensure our analyses accurately represent real-world threats and operating environments.

As a Space All-Source Intelligence Analyst, you will...

Acquire, analyze, and synthesize intelligence from multiple sources and classified disciplines to develop a comprehensive understanding of space threats and operational environments.
Translate qualitative intelligence assessments into quantitative data, variables, and parameters that can be incorporated into modeling, simulation, and analysis tools.
Collaborate with systems engineers and modelers to integrate intelligence into high-fidelity models used to assess and forecast national security space threats.
Apply intelligence insights to develop realistic operational and training scenarios for complex simulations.
Support model verification and validation by comparing simulation results with available real-world intelligence and identifying discrepancies that may affect model accuracy or fidelity.
Develop and maintain detailed threat and operational environment profiles to ensure models and simulations reflect the most current intelligence available.
Work closely with MS&A engineers, data scientists, analysts, and program managers to define intelligence requirements and effectively integrate intelligence throughout the modeling and analysis lifecycle.
Communicate intelligence findings and technical insights to multidisciplinary teams to support analyses, assessments, and sponsor needs.

Qualifications

You meet our minimum qualifications for the job if you...

B.S. in Intelligence Studies, Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, Data Science or equivalent experience.
At least 5 years of experience in DoD and IC-developed space systems, especially those systems focused on space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR), and space situational awareness (SSA)
Expert with IC and DoD processes and protocols for intelligence sharing and collaboration
Demonstrated experience conducting all-source analysis, data and intelligence synthesis, and intelligence analysis and production
Strong written and verbal communication skills with experience preparing executive-level reports, briefings, and intelligence-product publications
Hold an active TS/SCI security clearance. If selected, you will be subject to a government security clearance investigation and must meet the requirements for access to classified information. Eligibility requirements include U.S. citizenship.

You'll go above and beyond our minimum requirements if you...

Advanced degree in Intelligence Studies, National Security, National Strategy, Space Systems Engineering, or related STEM with 8+ years of relevant experience
Assignments to various IC organizations, with at least 3+ years at any one
Demonstrated experience working Space Weapons and Tactics
Experience in Red Team methodologies and threat analysis approaches
Participation in Space Warfare games (i.e., THORS HAMMER, Schriever Wargames, Space Flag)
Current TS//SCI clearance with polygraph, and with existing or previous access to SAP/CAP programs.

About Us

Why Work at APL?

The Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) brings world-class expertise to our nation’s most critical defense, security, space and science challenges. While we are dedicated to solving complex challenges and pioneering new technologies, what makes us truly outstanding is our culture. We offer a vibrant, welcoming atmosphere where you can bring your authentic self to work, continue to grow, and build strong connections with inspiring teammates.

At APL, we celebrate our differences of perspectives and encourage creativity and bold, new ideas. Vestmind is building an AI-powered decision layer to help individuals make smarter, clearer choices about their investments. new_jobs.description:
Description

Amazon is the most customer-centric company on Earth. We need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people who are passionate about doing the right thing.

We are looking for a Business Intelligence Analyst to join the Pricing & Payments team within Amazon's Last Mile Brazil organization, as part of the Partner Strategy & Experience (PSX) organization. This role owns the design, development, and maintenance of data intelligence solutions, automated mechanisms, and analytical frameworks that ensure pricing accuracy, payment reliability, and financial health across all delivery partner programs — EDSP (External Delivery Service Provider), AMPL (Amazon Partner Logistics), and AMXL (Amazon Extra Large).

As an Individual Contributor, you will be the data and automation backbone of the Payments & Pricing function — building pipelines, dashboards, reconciliation mechanisms, and self-service tools that eliminate manual processes, reduce payment errors, and provide real-time visibility into financial operations. You will partner closely with Payments Specialists, Pricing Specialists, Finance, and Operations to turn complex data into actionable intelligence.

This role reports directly to the Pricing & Payments Manager and works cross-functionally with Finance, Operations, Technology, and partner-facing teams.

This position is based out of an AMZL office.

If you are passionate about building intelligent data solutions, automating complex processes, and driving financial precision through analytics, come join our team.

Key job responsibilities

Design, build, and maintain automated data pipelines and ETL processes that support payment reconciliation, pricing validation, and financial reporting across all partner programs

Develop and maintain SQL-based queries, views, and stored procedures to extract, transform, and analyze large-scale operational and financial datasets

Build and maintain dashboards and reporting mechanisms (QuickSight, Tableau, or equivalent) providing real-time visibility into payment status, pricing accuracy, disputes, and financial KPIs

Create automated reconciliation mechanisms that identify payment discrepancies, pricing errors, and anomalies before they impact partners — reducing manual intervention and improving trust

Develop self-service analytical tools that enable the Payments and Pricing team to access insights without requiring ad-hoc requests

Automate recurring reports and manual processes, driving efficiency gains across the Payments & Pricing function

Conduct deep-dive analyses on payment cycles, dispute patterns, incentive effectiveness, and pricing model performance to support data-driven decision-making

Build alerting and exception-handling mechanisms that proactively flag issues (e.g., payment delays, pricing inconsistencies, unusual dispute volumes)

Partner with Technology and Engineering teams to define data requirements, validate data sources, and ensure data quality and integrity

Support the development of pricing models and incentive simulations by providing historical data analysis, scenario modeling, and impact projections

Document all data solutions, pipelines, and mechanisms with clear technical specifications and operational runbooks

Present analytical findings and automation proposals to stakeholders, translating technical solutions into business value

A day in the life

Your day starts by checking the automated health monitors you built for the payment pipeline. An alert fires — a batch of AMPL partner payments shows a 3% discrepancy against expected values. You dive into the SQL query that powers the reconciliation engine, identify a data source lag from a route restructuring, and push a fix before the payment cycle closes.

Mid-morning, you join a sync with the Payments Specialists to review a new automated dispute detection mechanism you're piloting. The early results are promising: 40% of disputes that previously required manual review are now auto-classified and routed, saving 15+ hours per week.

Before lunch, you finalize a new QuickSight dashboard for the Pricing team — it visualizes incentive effectiveness across partner segments, showing which incentive structures drive the best delivery performance per Real invested. You walk the Pricing Specialist through the self-service filters and drill-down capabilities.

After lunch, you deep-dive into a request from the Ops Excellence Manager: they need historical payment data cross-referenced with partner Scorecard performance to validate a hypothesis about payment timeliness and delivery quality correlation. You build the query, visualize the results, and share a brief with your findings.

Late afternoon, you work on your current sprint priority: automating the monthly partner payment summary that currently takes 8 hours of manual work. You're building a Python script that pulls from three data sources, reconciles automatically, and generates the formatted output — target: zero manual hours by next month.

You close the day documenting the new pipeline you deployed this week and updating the team's automation roadmap with next quarter's priorities.

About The Team

The Business Intelligence Analyst sits within the Pricing & Payments team, part of Amazon Logistics' Partner Strategy & Experience (PSX) organization. The Pricing & Payments function owns one of PSX's core pillars: "Pricing accuracy, incentive effectiveness, and payment reliability: ensuring financial health and trust across all delivery channels."

The team manages pricing models, payment cycles, incentive structures, and dispute resolution for +30 logistics partners across Brazil. The BI Analyst is the technical engine of this function — building the data infrastructure, automations, and intelligence that enable the team to operate at scale with precision and speed.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience in Business, Engineering, Supply Chain, Transportation, Mathematics, Economics, Physics or another technical field
Knowledge of writing and optimizing SQL queries in a business environment with large-scale, complex datasets
Experience building data pipelines or automated ETL processes
Experience with reporting and Data Visualization tools such as Quick Sight / Tableau / Power BI or other BI packages
Experience with data scripting languages (e.g., SQL, Python, R, or equivalent) or statistical/mathematical software (e.g., R, SAS, Matlab, or equivalent)
Experience in translating business needs into detailed feature requirements
Experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities, or experience in SQL Server/MySQL
Experience communicating technical concepts to non-technical audiences
Experience in communication and presentation skills, both written and verbal in Portuguese & English

Preferred Qualifications

Speak, write, and read fluently in English
Experience with financial services, payments or e-commerce
Experience with creating automated alarms, reports and KPI metrics for plant management
Knowledge of finance, accounting, business or related field focused on analytics
Experience working with Git or an equivalent distributed version control system
Experience in program management, logistics, operations, supply chain, transportation, or equivalent
Experience automating routine tasks
Knowledge of data structures, data modeling, and database schema
Master's degree in Math, Statistics, Computer Science, or related science field, or Master's degree and 2+ years of data scientist experience
Experience in Amazon Redshift and other AWS technologies

Job Summary

This position is located in the Department of Health (DC Health), Community Health Administration (CHA), Health Promotion and Disease Prevention Bureau (HPDP). DC Health promotes health, wellness, and equity across the District, and protects the safety of residents, visitors, and those doing business in the nation’s capital. DC Health believes that all people - no matter their race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, education level, age, language, religion, ability, or geographic location - should have the opportunity to live healthy lives. 

The Food Policy Data Analyst will support the Food Policy Council in building a data-driven understanding of the District’s food system. The position will establish indicators, data sources, and tools needed to monitor the food system over time, build and maintain public-facing dashboards that track key metrics across food access, the local food economy, supply chain, and other Food Policy Council priority areas. The position will work closely with District agencies, Food Policy Council members, and community partners to ensure food system data is accurate, accessible and used to inform program and policy decisions.

Duties And Responsibilities

Utilizes databases of information to create program reports, assures integrity of data, and utilizes software programs for retrieval of historical data, requests for information, summary reports and ad hoc analyses. Develops approaches and prepares analytical reports on performance measures, goals, milestones, trends, and improvements. Compiles trend data for required quarterly reporting and participates in management review of reported data and trends. Provides guidance and assists in the implementation of data-sharing with stakeholders, internal and external to DCH. Interprets and applies analytical techniques to procedures to enhance processing, reporting and query capabilities to improve efficiency and accuracy.

Captures, develops, and documents data definitions, rules, data quality requirements, and logical and physical data models based on program requirements. Performs data cleaning and data validation and verification. Determines the most effective approach to data collection and validation, and works independently to obtain needed data. Develops and applies analytical techniques to assist the agency in meeting its grant/research reporting and analysis and value-added intelligence product development objectives. Ensures the quality of deliverables (processes, procedures, reports, data extracts, audit logs) related to requirements, design, implementation, testing, and adherence to reporting standards.

Qualifications And Education

Specialized
Experience:

Build an Aviation Career You’re Proud Of
